chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, altogether, from Ibn Mahboub from Umar ibn Yazeed who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who intended to emancipate a slave of his, and his master had taken from him a tax that he had imposed upon him every year. The master was pleased with that, and the slave was pleased with that. So the slave acquired wealth in his trade besides what he used to give to his master from the tax. He (peace be upon him) said: 'When he pays to his master what was imposed upon him, then whatever he acquires after the imposition is for the slave.'

Then Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Is it not that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has imposed obligations upon the servants? So when they fulfill them to Him, He does not question them about what is besides that.' I said to him, 'So what do you think regarding the slave if he gives in charity from what he has acquired and emancipates (a slave) after the obligation which he used to pay to his master?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, that is obligatory for him.'

I said, 'If the slave emancipates (a slave) from what he has acquired besides the obligation, for whom will be the guardianship (wala') of the emancipated one?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He goes and the guardianship attaches to whomever he likes. So when he guarantees his blood-money (diyah) and his compensation, he becomes his master and inherits him.'

I said to him, 'Did not the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) say: 'The guardianship is for the one who emancipates?'' He (peace be upon him) said: 'This is a free person (sa'ibah), his guardianship does not belong to a slave like him.' I said, 'If the slave who emancipated him guarantees his blood-money and his actions, does that bind him, and he becomes his master and inherits him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'That is not permissible, and a slave does not inherit a free man.'

key_terms.سَائِبَة: A free person, specifically one emancipated by a master
key_terms.ضَرِيبَة: Tax or fixed tribute imposed by the master
key_terms.وَلَاء: Guardianship or lineage right following emancipation

ai.seo_question: What are the financial rights and inheritance rules for a slave who pays a fixed tax to his master?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) draws a parallel between divine law and manumission economics, arguing that just as Allah accepts obligatory duties and does not demand excess, a master should accept the fixed tax and allow the slave to retain surplus earnings. This hadith is pivotal in Shia jurisprudence for establishing the slave's financial autonomy and clarifying the distinction between 'wala'' (lineage of manumission) and inheritance, specifically noting that a slave cannot inherit from a free person even if he guarantees their blood money. The Imam refutes the general maxim 'wala' belongs to the emancipator' in this specific context, emphasizing that the slave's emancipation of another creates a contractual bond of liability rather than automatic inheritance rights.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, altogether, from Ibn Mahboub, from Umar Bin Yazeed who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a man who intended to emancipated an owned slave of his, and his master had taken from him his earnings, which he had enforced upon him during every year. The master was pleased with that, and the slave was pleased with that. So the slave achieved wealth in his business besides what he used to give to his master, from the earning. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When he has paid off to his master what was necessitated upon him, so whatever he achieved after the enforcement, so it is for the slave’.

Then Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Is it not that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic has Obligated the Obligations upon the servants. So when they fulfill these to Him<sup>azwj</sup>, He<sup>azwj</sup> does not Question them about what is besides that’. I said, ‘So what is your<sup>asws</sup> view, is it for the slave if he were to give in charity from what he earns, and he emancipates (a slave) after the enforced (amount) which he used to pay to his master?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, that (payment) is Obligated upon him’.

I said, ‘So if the slave were to emancipate (a slave) from what he has earned besides the enforced (payment), so for whom would be the guardianship of the emancipated slave?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would go and give his guardianship to the one he so likes to. So when he takes the responsibility of his crimes, and his intellect, he would be his master, and would inherit him’.

I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Did not Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> say: ‘The guardianship is for the one who emancipates?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He is an emancipated slave, his guardianship does not happen to be for a slave like him’. I said, ‘Supposing the slave were to take the responsibility for the one who emancipated him, for his crimes, and his actions, would that necessitate him, and he would become his master and inherit him?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘That is not allowed, and a slave would not inherit a free man’.
